title: Goemans-Williamson 0.878-Approximation for MaxCut
description: Formalization of the Goemans-Williamson (1995) semidefinite programming approach to MaxCut, achieving an approximation ratio of α_GW ≈ 0.878 via hyperplane rounding of SDP relaxation.

overview.historicalContext:
The Goemans-Williamson algorithm (1995) was a landmark result in combinatorial optimization, achieving a 0.878-approximation ratio for the Maximum Cut problem using semidefinite programming (SDP). This substantially improved the simple randomized 1/2-approximation.

The key insight is to relax the integer programming formulation of MaxCut to a semidefinite program, where each vertex is assigned a unit vector on a high-dimensional sphere instead of a binary ±1 value. The SDP can be solved in polynomial time, and a random hyperplane is used to round the continuous solution back to a discrete cut.

Remarkably, under the Unique Games Conjecture (Khot et al. 2007), α_GW ≈ 0.878 is the best possible approximation ratio achievable in polynomial time, making this algorithm conditionally optimal.
overview.problemStatement:
Given a graph $G = (V, E)$, the **MaxCut** problem asks to partition $V$ into two sets to maximize edges crossing between them.

The **SDP relaxation** assigns unit vectors $v_i \in S^n$ to each vertex and maximizes:
$$\text{SDP}_{\text{OPT}} = \frac{1}{2} \sum_{(i,j) \in E} (1 - v_i \cdot v_j)$$

**Hyperplane rounding**: Choose random $r \in S^n$; assign vertex $i$ to side A if $v_i \cdot r \geq 0$.

The probability that edge $(i,j)$ is cut equals $\frac{\arccos(v_i \cdot v_j)}{\pi}$.

The key inequality: for all $x \in [-1,1]$,
$$\frac{\arccos(x)}{\pi} \geq \alpha_{\text{GW}} \cdot \frac{1-x}{2}$$
where $\alpha_{\text{GW}} = \min_{0 < \theta \leq \pi} \frac{2}{\pi} \cdot \frac{\theta}{1 - \cos\theta} \approx 0.878$.
overview.text: Formalization of the Goemans-Williamson (1995) semidefinite programming approach to MaxCut, achieving an approximation ratio of α_GW ≈ 0.878 via hyperplane rounding of SDP relaxation.
overview.proofStrategy:
The formalization captures the algebraic structure of the GW approximation guarantee:

1. **Cut infrastructure**: Reuse the Cut partition structure from the 1/2-approximation proof

2. **SDP relaxation** (axiomatized): Define SDP_OPT as an axiom satisfying MaxCut ≤ SDP_OPT

3. **GW constant**: Define α_GW = 878/1000 as a conservative rational lower bound

4. **Rounding inequality** (axiomatized): E[|C|] ≥ α_GW · SDP_OPT

5. **Main theorem** (proved): Chain the inequalities:
$$\alpha_{\text{GW}} \cdot \text{MaxCut} \leq \alpha_{\text{GW}} \cdot \text{SDP}_{\text{OPT}} \leq \mathbb{E}[|C|]$$

The axioms cleanly separate the SDP infrastructure (which Mathlib lacks) from the algebraic proof chain (which is fully verified).
keyInsights: The SDP relaxation is a natural upper bound on MaxCut: any cut embeds as a feasible SDP solution with v_i = ±e₁.
The GW constant α_GW ≈ 0.878 is the minimum of θ/(π(1-cos θ)/2) over θ ∈ (0,π], achieved at θ* ≈ 2.331 radians.
Hyperplane rounding preserves at least α_GW fraction of the SDP value, giving the approximation guarantee.
The conservative bound 878/1000 < true α_GW ensures all inequalities remain valid.
Under the Unique Games Conjecture, no polynomial-time algorithm can beat this ratio, making it conditionally optimal.

sections.title: Setup and Imports
sections.summary: Import Mathlib modules for graphs, real numbers, and finite sets.
sections.mathContext: MaxCut: partition V to maximize crossing edges. NP-hard. Approximation algorithms are key.

sections.title: Cut Infrastructure
sections.summary: Define GWCut structure and MaxCut value, mirroring the 1/2-approximation proof.
sections.mathContext: MaxCut(G) = max over partitions of crossing edge count. Random partition: E[cut] >= |E|/2 >= MaxCut/2.

sections.title: The GW Constant
sections.summary: Define α_GW = 878/1000 and prove key bounds (0 < α_GW < 1, α_GW > 1/2).
sections.mathContext: alpha_GW = min over [-1,1] of arccos(x)/(pi(1-x)/2) ~ 0.878. Worst-case GW rounding ratio.

sections.title: SDP Relaxation
sections.summary: Axiomatize the SDP relaxation value and its relationship to MaxCut.
sections.mathContext: SDP relaxation: replace x_i in {+-1} with unit vectors v_i. Maximize sum (1-v_i.v_j)/2 over edges.

sections.title: Hyperplane Rounding
sections.summary: Axiomatize the expected cut from GW hyperplane rounding.
sections.mathContext: GW rounding: random hyperplane r, set x_i = sgn(v_i . r). Pr[x_i != x_j] = arccos(v_i.v_j)/pi.

sections.title: The GW Inequality
sections.summary: Axiomatize the core analytical result: E[cut] ≥ α_GW · SDP_OPT.
sections.mathContext: Core: E[cut] >= alpha_GW * SDP_OPT >= alpha_GW * MaxCut.

sections.title: Main Theorem: 0.878-Approximation
sections.summary: Prove the main result: α_GW · MaxCut ≤ E[GW cut], with ratio bound corollary.
sections.mathContext: Goemans-Williamson (1995): 0.878-approximation for MaxCut. Best polynomial-time ratio under UGC.

sections.title: Structural Bounds
sections.summary: Prove MaxCut ≤ edges and expected cut ≤ edges bounds.
sections.mathContext: MaxCut <= |E|. E[GW cut] <= |E|. Bipartite: MaxCut = |E| (all edges cross).

sections.title: Arccos Rounding Probability Framework
sections.summary: Define roundingProb(x) = arccos(x)/π and sdpContrib(x) = (1-x)/2 using Mathlib's arccos. Prove boundary values at x = -1, 0, 1 and range properties [0,1].
sections.mathContext: Rounding prob: arccos(v_i.v_j)/pi. SDP contrib: (1-v_i.v_j)/2. Ratio >= alpha_GW for all inner products.

sections.title: GW Inequality at Boundary Points
sections.summary: Prove the GW inequality αGW · sdpContrib(x) ≤ roundingProb(x) at the three critical points x = -1, 0, 1.
sections.mathContext: GW ratio achieves minimum alpha_GW at inner product t* ~ -0.689. Verified by calculus.

sections.title: Ratio Analysis
sections.summary: Analyze the GW ratio roundingProb(x)/sdpContrib(x) at boundary points, showing it equals 1 at x = 0 and x = -1.
sections.mathContext: At t=-1: ratio = 1. At t=0: ratio = 1. At t=1: limit = 1 (0/0). Min at interior t*.

sections.title: Enhanced Structural Bounds
sections.summary: Additional bounds: improvement factor over random, bipartite specialization, tighter αGW estimates, and UGC hardness axiom.
sections.mathContext: Improvement: alpha_GW/0.5 ~ 1.756x over random. Bipartite: ratio 1. Triangle: ratio ~ 0.912.

conclusion.summary:
This formalization captures the algebraic backbone of the celebrated Goemans-Williamson MaxCut approximation. The SDP infrastructure is cleanly axiomatized (Mathlib has no SDP support), while the core proof chain—from SDP relaxation through rounding inequality to approximation guarantee—is fully verified.

The formalization demonstrates how axiomatization can be used productively: by clearly separating the verified algebraic argument from the axiomatized analytical/optimization components, we achieve a rigorous proof of the key result while honestly marking what remains unformalized.
conclusion.implications:
**Theoretical Significance**: **Algorithmic Impact**

The GW result transformed combinatorial optimization by demonstrating that semidefinite programming relaxations could yield dramatic improvements over simpler approaches (0.878 vs 0.5). This launched an entire research program of SDP-based approximation algorithms.

**Conditional Optimality**

Under the Unique Games Conjecture (Khot 2002, Khot et al.

2007), no polynomial-time algorithm can achieve an approximation ratio better than α_GW for MaxCut. This means the GW algorithm is essentially the best possible.

**Formalization Frontier**

Full formalization of the SDP components would require:
- Semidefinite programming theory in Lean/Mathlib
- Measure theory on the unit sphere (for hyperplane rounding)
- The arccos inequality via calculus of variations.
openQuestions: Can we formalize the SDP relaxation infrastructure in Lean (positive semidefinite cones, duality)?
Can the arccos inequality arccos(x)/π ≥ α_GW·(1-x)/2 be proved using Lean's calculus library?
Can we formalize the Unique Games Conjecture hardness result showing α_GW is optimal?
What about extending to weighted MaxCut or MAX-2SAT via the same SDP approach?

crossReferences.description: The simple 1/2-approximation via independent random assignment. The GW algorithm improves this from 0.5 to 0.878 by using SDP-guided correlations between vertex assignments

MaxCut is NP-hard, so exact polynomial-time solutions are unlikely. The GW algorithm achieves the best possible polynomial-time approximation (under UGC), illustrating how approximation algorithms circumvent NP-hardness
The Cauchy-Schwarz inequality underpins the SDP relaxation: inner products v_i . v_j of unit vectors satisfy |v_i . v_j| <= 1, and the SDP optimizes over these inner products
